*In character as the farmer:*

Well, let me think about this year. I'm 70, my wife is the only other person at home, and after fifty years on this land I know every corner of these six mu. My legs aren't what they were, but I went through senior high back in the day and I still keep a little notebook where I write down what I planted, what I put on it, and what I pulled off each plot. That's how I know, for example, that my south plot needs a bit less nitrogen than the north — soil there holds fertility better after years of manure.

With just two of us, labor is the real bottleneck, not land. I can't handle six mu of cabbage and chili at once — the picking would kill me. So I plan my calendar carefully, stagger the crops, and keep the labor-hungry things like chili to one mu.

Here's how I'm laying it out:

- **3 mu on my main rotation** (cabbage → maize → spinach). This is my bread-and-butter: spring head cabbage (甘蓝) for the May market, summer maize in the gap, then spinach going in early October for winter and early spring harvest. The maize isn't really for profit — it's the soil rest and the stover for the neighbor's goats in exchange for some manure.
- **1 mu of Chinese cabbage (白菜)** planted in early August for the November pickling season. Quzhou people buy a lot of Chinese cabbage this time of year.
- **1 mu of chili**, transplanted late April. Highest return per mu I grow, but also the most picking. I can just about manage one mu with my wife helping.
- **1 mu of kidney beans**, summer planting. Half for our own eating, half to sell dry. Beans are easy on me — they fix their own nitrogen, so I barely fertilize them, and I can harvest a few rows at a time.

On fertilizer: I learned long ago you don't dump it all at planting. I split for everything except spinach (too short a crop). For cabbage and Chinese cabbage I put a compound fertilizer 15-15-15 down as base, then urea topdress when they start heading. For maize I do base + big-belly stage. I use the well for irrigation but pumping costs real money — about 15-20 yuan per mu per round — so I only water when the crop truly needs it, not on a fixed schedule.

I don't buy much pesticide. For cabbage I do one spray for cabbage worm (青虫) in May, and chili needs a couple of sprays for aphids. Everything else I can manage by hand or just accept some loss.

Budget-wise, I've got maybe 4,000-4,500 yuan set aside for inputs. That's tight but doable if I don't get greedy on fertilizer.
